hello.note: Reply: ওয়ালাইকুম আসসালাম (walaikum assalam). Hindus and West Bengal use নমস্কার (nomoshkar).

goodbye.note: When you leave: আসি (ashi), 'I'll be off'. In Bangladesh also আল্লাহ হাফেজ (allah hafez).

please.note: Used sparingly; politeness mostly comes from the verb ending, e.g. বসুন (boshun), 'please sit'.

thank_you.note: Said less than in English; with friends and family it can even sound distant.

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'it's no matter'. Bengali has no set reply to thanks; this is the natural one.

yes.note: A nasal 'hæ' sound. Politer, especially in Bangladesh: জি (ji).

no.note: Politer, especially in Bangladesh: জি না (ji na).

sorry.note: English সরি (sori) is just as common day to day. For a bigger apology: মাফ করবেন (maf korben).

excuse_me.note: Literally 'are you listening?'. People often add ভাই (bhai) to a man, আপা/দিদি (apa/didi) to a woman.

good_morning.note: Rather formal. Day to day people use the normal greeting or English গুড মর্নিং (gud morning).

how_are_you.note: To a friend: কেমন আছ? (kemon achho?)

im_fine.note: Often shortened to ভালো, আপনি? (bhalo, apni?), 'fine, and you?'

my_name_is.note: No word for 'is' is needed here.

nice_to_meet_you.text: আপনার সাথে পরিচিত হয়ে ভালো লাগল
nice_to_meet_you.roman: apnar shathe porichito hoye bhalo laglo
nice_to_meet_you.note: In West Bengal সঙ্গে (shonge) is more usual than সাথে (shathe).

where_from.note: Between Bengalis: আপনার বাড়ি কোথায়? (apnar bari kothay?), asking about their home town.

speak_english.note: কি (ki) here just marks a yes/no question.

dont_understand.note: Shorter: বুঝলাম না (bujhlam na), 'I didn't get that'.

speak_slowly.note: Softer: একটু ধীরে বলবেন? (ektu dhire bolben?), 'would you speak a bit slowly?'

what.note: Spelled কী for 'what'; কি (same sound) is the yes/no question marker.

when.note: For which day or date: কবে? (kobe?)

who.note: For more than one person: কারা? (kara?)

how_much.note: At a market, just এটা কত? (eta koto?)

where_bathroom.note: Literally 'can you tell me where the bathroom is?'. টয়লেট (toylet) is also common.

what_time.note: In Bangladesh often কয়টা বাজে? (koyta baje?)

one.note: Digit: ১. When counting things add -টা: একটা (ekta).

two.note: Digit: ২. With things: দুটো (duto), in Bangladesh দুইটা (duita).

water.note: In West Bengal and among Hindus: জল (jol).

tea.note: Usually milky and sweet. Black tea: রং চা (rong cha) in Bangladesh, লিকার চা (likar cha) in West Bengal.

bread.note: Means flatbread (chapati). Sliced loaf bread is পাউরুটি (pauruti).

im_hungry.note: In Bangladesh also: আমার ক্ষুধা লেগেছে (amar khudha legechhe).

menu_please.note: The polite 'will you…?' ending (-ben) does the job of 'please'.

delicious.note: Everyday: খুব মজা হয়েছে! (khub moja hoyechhe!) in Bangladesh, দারুণ খেতে! (darun khete!) in West Bengal.

no_meat.note: Fish doesn't count as meat in Bengal; add মাছও খাই না (machho khai na) if you avoid it too.

enjoy_meal.note: No set phrase exists; hosts say this, 'eat your fill'. Muslims say বিসমিল্লাহ (bismillah) before eating.

left.note: Literally 'to the left side'. In Bangladesh often বাম দিকে (bam dike).

straight_ahead.note: In directions often just সোজা যান (shoja jan), 'go straight'.

stop_here.note: Also natural: এখানে নামিয়ে দিন (ekhane namiye din), 'drop me here'.

airport.note: In speech, এয়ারপোর্ট (eyarport) is just as common.

hotel.note: হোটেল can also mean a cheap eatery; for a place to stay say আবাসিক হোটেল (abashik hotel).

want_to_go.note: To a rickshaw or taxi driver: … যাবেন? (… jaben?), 'will you go to …?'

too_expensive.note: To bargain: একটু কম করুন (ektu kom korun), 'bring it down a little'.

id_like_this.note: Or simply এটা দিন (eta din), 'give me this'.

cash.note: In shops people often just say ক্যাশ (kyash).

big.note: ড় is a quick flapped r with the tongue curled back.

tomorrow.note: In speech just কাল (kal), which also means yesterday; the verb tense tells them apart.

yesterday.note: In speech just কাল (kal), same as 'tomorrow'; the past-tense verb makes it clear.

good_evening.note: Formal; in daily life the normal greeting is used at any hour.

good_night.note: Formal; with friends English গুড নাইট (gud nait) is more usual.

wait_moment.note: Literally 'stand a little'. Also: এক মিনিট (ek minit); formal: একটু অপেক্ষা করুন (ektu opekkha korun).

help.note: Literally 'save (me)!'. Also: কেউ সাহায্য করুন! (keu shahajjo korun!), 'someone help!'

call_police.note: Emergency number: 999 in Bangladesh, 112 in India.

pharmacy.note: Signs usually say ফার্মেসি (farmesi), a word everyone uses.

allergic.note: Attach -তে or -এ to the allergen: চিংড়িতে (chingrite) 'to shrimp', বাদামে (badame) 'to nuts'.

be_careful.note: As a parting 'take care': সাবধানে থাকবেন (shabdhane thakben).

i_like_it.note: For something you just tried: ভালো লেগেছে (bhalo legechhe). Also: এটা আমার পছন্দ (eta amar pochhondo).

im_tired.note: Everyday: আমার খুব ক্লান্ত লাগছে (amar khub klanto lagchhe), 'I feel really tired'.

welcome.note: The warm spoken welcome, 'come in, come in!'. On signs and in speeches: স্বাগতম (shagotom).

my_family.note: In everyday talk also আমার বাড়ির লোকজন (amar barir lokjon), 'my folks at home'.

mother.note: In Bangladesh children often say আম্মু (ammu) or আম্মা (amma).

father.note: In Bangladesh children often say আব্বু (abbu) or আব্বা (abba).

brother.note: Older brother: বড় ভাই (boro bhai); in West Bengal দাদা (dada). ভাই also addresses any man.

sister.note: Older sister: আপা (apa) in Bangladesh, দিদি (didi) in West Bengal.

child.note: Son: ছেলে (chhele), daughter: মেয়ে (meye). For a young child people say বাচ্চা (bachcha).

friend.note: A female friend: বান্ধবী (bandhobi), though বন্ধু (bondhu) is also used for women.

this_is_my_friend.note: For a woman: ও আমার বান্ধবী (o amar bandhobi). For someone older, ইনি (ini) instead of ও (o).

are_you_married.note: Formal: আপনি কি বিবাহিত? (apni ki bibahito?)

have_children.note: Also common: বাচ্চাকাচ্চা (bachchakachcha) instead of ছেলেমেয়ে.

monday.note: Every day name ends in -বার (bar), 'day'. On Monday: সোমবারে (shombare).

thursday.note: In speech often shortened to বিষ্যুদবার (bisshudbar).

weekend.note: In speech often উইকেন্ড (uikend). Bangladesh's Fri–Sat weekend is the সাপ্তাহিক ছুটি (shaptahik chhuti).

what_day.note: For the date: আজ কত তারিখ? (aj koto tarikh?)

next_week.note: Everyday: সামনের সপ্তাহে (shamner shoptahe). The ending -এ (-e) means 'in'.

twenty.note: Digits: ২০. Also কুড়ি (kuri), especially in West Bengal.

thirty.note: Digits: ৩০. In West Bengal usually তিরিশ (tirish).

thousand.note: Digits: ১০০০. Bigger: লাখ (lakh) = 100,000 and কোটি (koti) = 10 million.

how_old.note: To a child: তোমার বয়স কত? (tomar boyosh koto?)

years_old.note: E.g. আমার বয়স ত্রিশ বছর (amar boyosh trish bochhor). No -টা on the number here.

what_colour.note: Also: এটার রং কী? (etar rong ki?)

this_one.note: When pointing, often stressed as এইটা (eita).

that_one.note: When pointing, often stressed as ওইটা (oita).

another_one.note: Softer: আরেকটা দেবেন? (arekta deben?), 'would you give me another?'

its_hot.note: 'I feel hot': আমার গরম লাগছে (amar gorom lagchhe).

its_cold.note: 'I feel cold': আমার ঠান্ডা লাগছে (amar thanda lagchhe).

its_sunny.note: রোদ (rod) is sunshine. Harsh midday sun: কড়া রোদ (kora rod).

its_windy.note: In West Bengal: খুব হাওয়া দিচ্ছে (khub hawa dichchhe).

beautiful_day.note: As an exclamation: কী সুন্দর দিন! (ki shundor din!)

summer.note: Formal: গ্রীষ্মকাল (grisshokal). Bengal counts six seasons; the rainy one is বর্ষা (borsha).

winter.note: In speech often just শীত (shit), which also means 'cold'.

have_reservation.text: আমার একটা রুম বুক করা আছে
have_reservation.roman: amar ekta rum buk kora achhe
have_reservation.note: Also: আমার বুকিং আছে (amar buking achhe).

room.note: The usual word in hotels. A room in a home is ঘর (ghor).

next_train.note: Literally 'when will the next train leave?'. Shorter: পরের ট্রেন কটায়? (porer tren kotay?)

is_this_seat_free.note: Also: এখানে কেউ বসেছে? (ekhane keu boshechhe?), 'is anyone sitting here?'

what_do_you_do.note: Formal: আপনার পেশা কী? (apnar pesha ki?)

i_work_in.note: Add -এ/-তে to the place: ব্যাংকে (byangke). For a salaried job also: চাকরি করি (chakri kori).

im_student.note: A woman says: আমি ছাত্রী (ami chhatri).

im_busy.note: Softer: এখন একটু ব্যস্ত আছি (ekhon ektu byasto achhi), 'a bit busy right now'.

day_off.note: 'I'm off today': আজ আমার ছুটি (aj amar chhuti).

colleague.note: Used for men and women alike. In offices also কলিগ (kolig).

lets_start.note: With friends: চলো, শুরু করি (cholo, shuru kori).

good_job.note: Literally 'it came out great!'. Praising the person: খুব ভালো করেছেন! (khub bhalo korechhen!)

table_for_two.note: Literally 'will there be a table for two?'

what_recommend.note: Also very common: আপনাদের এখানে কী ভালো? (apnader ekhane ki bhalo?), 'what's good here?'

not_spicy.note: ঝাল (jhal) is chilli heat. 'Less spicy': ঝাল কম দেবেন (jhal kom deben).

vegetarian_food.note: Fish and eggs are not নিরামিষ (niramish); dishes with them are আমিষ (amish).

more_water.note: In West Bengal and among Hindus: আরেকটু জল দেবেন? (arektu jol deben?)

no_sugar.note: Tea comes sweet unless you ask. 'Less sugar': চিনি কম (chini kom).

im_full.note: Hosts insist on second helpings; add আর না (ar na), 'no more', to refuse politely.

it_was_delicious.note: Warmer, to a host: খুব তৃপ্তি করে খেলাম (khub tripti kore khelam), 'I ate with real pleasure'.

keep_change.note: In Bangladesh also: ভাংতিটা রেখে দিন (bhangtita rekhe din).

head_hurts.note: Also: আমার মাথা ধরেছে (amar matha dhorechhe).

medicine.note: Formal spelling, seen on signs and labels: ঔষধ (oushodh).

call_ambulance.note: Emergency number: 999 in Bangladesh, 112 in India.

dentist.note: Literally 'tooth doctor', what everyone says. Formal: দন্তচিকিৎসক (dontochikitshok).

need_rest.note: Casual: একটু রেস্ট নিতে হবে (ektu rest nite hobe).

feel_better.note: Also: আগের চেয়ে ভালো আছি (ager cheye bhalo achhi), 'better than before'.

get_well.note: To a friend: তাড়াতাড়ি সুস্থ হয়ে ওঠো! (taratari shustho hoye otho!)

lets_meet.note: With friends: চলো, দেখা করি (cholo, dekha kori).

are_you_free.note: Literally 'will you have time tomorrow?'. Also common: কাল ফ্রি আছেন? (kal fri achhen?)

call_me.note: To a friend: ফোন কোরো (fon koro); in Bangladesh ফোন দিও (fon dio).

your_number.note: Bengalis usually ask for a number with কত (koto), 'how much', rather than কী (ki).

have_nice_day.note: Not a traditional phrase; a very Bengali parting is ভালো থাকবেন (bhalo thakben), 'stay well'.

good_luck.note: In speech English গুড লাক (gud lak) is just as common.

happy_birthday.note: Just as common: হ্যাপি বার্থডে (hyapi barthde).

thanks_a_lot.note: Warmer still: অসংখ্য ধন্যবাদ (oshongkho dhonnobad), 'countless thanks'.

miss_you.note: Literally 'you keep coming to mind'. Also very common: তোমাকে মিস করছি (tomake mis korchhi).
